blocks.text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for clean, readable syntax. You write plain-English-like code, and Python's interpreter turns it into instructions the computer can run.

blocks.text: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and released in 1991. The name comes from the comedy group Monty Python — not the snake.
Python is one of the most in-demand languages in the world. Its simple syntax makes it a great first language, and it powers everything from websites to artificial intelligence.

blocks.text: Control flow lets your program make decisions. An if statement runs a block only when its condition is true; else handles everything else.

blocks.text: Loops repeat a block of code. A for loop walks through a sequence; each pass checks whether there is a next item, runs the body, and moves on.

blocks.alt: Loop cycle: check for next item, run the loop body, move to next item, repeat
blocks.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif"><defs><marker id="pyl-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="var(--text-muted)"/></marker></defs><rect x="110" y="14" width="120" height="38" rx="9" fill="var(--card)" stroke="var(--accent-indigo)" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="170" y="37" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--text)">Next item?</text><rect x="214" y="120" width="110" height="38" rx="9" fill="var(--card)" stroke="var(--accent-green)" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="269" y="143" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--text)">Run body</text><rect x="16" y="120" width="110" height="38" rx="9" fill="var(--card)" stroke="var(--accent-blue)" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="71" y="143" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--text)">Advance</text><path d="M210,44 C260,60 285,90 275,118" fill="none" stroke="var(--text-muted)" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#pyl-arrow)"/><path d="M214,142 L128,140" fill="none" stroke="var(--text-muted)" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#pyl-arrow)"/><path d="M64,118 C56,88 90,58 128,46" fill="none" stroke="var(--text-muted)" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#pyl-arrow)"/><text x="170" y="186" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="var(--text-muted)">Repeat until no items remain</text></svg>
blocks.sideText: When there are no more items, the loop ends and the program continues below it.

blocks.text: Test what you learned in this module:

questions.question: How do you print text to the screen in Python?
questions.explanation: print() is Python's built-in function for displaying output. echo and printf belong to other languages; console.log is JavaScript.

questions.question: What type does the value 3.14 have in Python?
questions.explanation: Numbers with a decimal point are floats. Whole numbers like 25 are ints, and True/False are bools.

questions.question: Which keyword runs a block only when a condition is false?
questions.explanation: else handles the case when the if condition is False. elif checks an additional condition; then and otherwise aren't Python keywords.

questions.question: What does a function's return statement do?
options: Prints a value to the screen
Sends a result back to whoever called the function
questions.explanation: return hands a value back to the caller, so you can store or use the result. It ends the function, not the whole program.

blocks.text: That's the foundation of Python! From here you can move on to strings, lists, and building real programs.
